message.content:
Research task for Nxeon (game/VPS hosting platform, code at /opt/nxeon, TypeScript/Next.js/Prisma). The owner wants to know which game-server titles/options competitors sell that Nxeon does NOT currently offer, so they can decide what to add to the catalog.

Step 1 — establish Nxeon's current catalog: read /opt/nxeon/lib/games.ts and /opt/nxeon/lib/game-config.ts (grep for GAME_META or similar) to get the definitive, current list of game families Nxeon sells hosting for. Don't guess from memory — read the actual file.

Step 2 — research these three competitor game-hosting pages the owner just pointed at, via WebFetch:
- https://ultahost.com/gaming-hosting
- https://www.bisecthosting.com/game-server-hosting
- https://shockbyte.com/games
List every distinct game title each competitor offers hosting for (these sites usually have a grid/list of game logos or a games page — if the top-level URL doesn't show the full list, look for a "view all games" or games-index link on the page and fetch that too).

Step 3 — diff: produce a list of games these competitors sell that are NOT in Nxeon's current catalog (from Step 1). Group by how many of the 3 competitors offer it (e.g. "offered by all 3", "offered by 2/3", "offered by 1/3") as a rough signal of how mainstream/in-demand the title is. Note any title that appears especially frequently across all three (likely worth prioritizing).

Step 4 — flag anything from Steam/SteamCMD app IDs would be needed (if you can tell from the competitor page or general knowledge) versus games that need a fully custom/proprietary server binary (harder to add) — this matters for how much engineering effort each addition would take, but keep this brief, just a one-word estimate (Steam/Custom/Unknown) per game if you can tell.

Output: a single markdown table — Game | Offered by (count/3, which ones) | Engine/install type (Steam/Custom/Unknown) — sorted by how many competitors offer it, descending. Keep total report under 700 words including the table. This is research only — do not write or edit any code, and do not touch lib/games.ts.
